LM Studio's agentic workflow platform can now run tasks using Kimi K3, a model from Moonshot AI with 2.8 trillion parameters and a 1 million token context window. Read on for details.

Kimi K3 is now available on LM Studio Bionic

A few days ago, LM Studio announced Bionic, a new application designed for users who want to run agentic tasks with open-source models.

Bionic is designed to handle tasks ranging from coding and research to more complex document and file editing work.

Users can run models locally, or when a task requires more computational power, call on larger cloud-based open-source models that offer longer context windows, stronger reasoning, and tool-use capabilities that smaller local models currently cannot match.

The following is an excerpt from LM Studio's original announcement:

As for cloud-based models, Bionic uses inference services based in the United States and implements a zero data retention policy. This means all requests are processed on U.S. servers, and prompts, files, and model outputs are not stored after processing is complete.

As of now, users accessing cloud-based open-source models can choose from DeepSeek V4, Pro, GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.6, and Kimi-K2.7-Code. The company added Kimi K3 today, giving users access to what many consider to be the most powerful open-source model currently available.

Through Bionic, Kimi K3 is priced at $3 per million input tokens, $0.30 per million cached input tokens, and $15 per million output tokens.

This pricing stands in stark contrast to previous models—earlier models charged between $0.95 and $1.74 per million input tokens and between $3.48 and $4.50 per million output tokens.

That said, the addition of Kimi K3 is still a welcome development, especially for users looking to tackle more demanding tasks through LM Studio Bionic.

LM Studio Bionic is available for Mac and Windows platforms. Click here for more details.
